name: Tie clip / tie bar

card.summary: A tie clip is a small metal bar that fastens a tie to the shirt so it hangs straight and the outfit looks neater.
card.aka: tie bar; tie clasp; tie slide

quick.overview:
A tie clip, also called a tie bar or tie clasp, holds a necktie against the shirt front so it does not swing or flip around. It looks like a small decorative bar across the tie.

The payoff is a tidier, more finished formal look. It became popular in the 1920s with thin silk ties and remains a menswear accessory; there is no research on it as an appearance tool.
quick.how: Wearers clip it across the tie and shirt placket. Grokipedia describes the usual position as a few inches below the knot, and clips come in metals such as silver, gold or brass.
quick.risks: No health risks; a clip can mark delicate fabric if worn too tight, and overly ornate designs may look out of place in conservative settings.

lead: A tie clip, tie bar or tie clasp is a small, usually metal accessory that fastens a necktie to the shirt front.[1][2] It stops the tie from swinging or dangling and adds a decorative accent.[2]
It became popular in the 1920s with thin silk ties and largely replaced the older tie pin.[1] In the United States a tie clip is one of the few pieces of jewellery service members may wear.[1]
No clinical or scientific studies have examined tie clips as an appearance aid.

chain: Clip holds tie flat against shirt
Outfit looks neater and more finished
angle.text: The clip keeps the tie in place so the outfit stays tidy through the day and adds a small metal accent.

infobox: A few inches below the knot, per Grokipedia

paras: The modern clip has a spring-loaded jaw that grips tie and shirt without piercing, unlike tie tacks or pins that go through the fabric.[2] Many carry engraving, monograms or club badges.[1][2]

Tie pins and stick pins preceded the clip in the nineteenth century.[2] Straight silk ties became fashionable in the 1920s and made non-piercing clips preferable, according to Grokipedia, which is AI-generated; it adds that the style surged after the Second World War and faded with casual dress in the 1960s and 70s.[2]

timeline.event: Tie clips become popular with thin silk ties.[1]
